Question: In a restaurant, what food have the greatest cost markups relative to the price of the ingredients?
Answer: In a restaurant, what foods have the greatest cost markups relative to the price of the ingredients? In a restaurant, the drinks usually have the highest markups. Sodas, coffee, teas, and lemonades are cheap to make (even with free refills) and give a good return. Alcohol also has a high markup. Beers, wines, and alcoholic beverages bring in a lot of money. The average restaurant charges $3-$5 for a beer, $5-$10 for wine, and $5-$10 for alcohol. Knowing the prices for these things in the stores makes it easy to see why so many restaurants push their servers and bartenders to make alcohol sales a priority. Restaurants also mark up appetizers, sides, salads, and desserts more than the actual meals. These things are extras that enhance a meal, so servers also do their best to sell them to customers. The average return on an average meal is $2-$4 dollars, most of which goes into operating costs like supplies, wages, bills, and more food. Although restaurants save money by buying in bulk, there are still high costs associated with running a restaurant. Most of the highest markups are on anything extra for the meal.

Question: Was Jesus Christ an immigrant or a refugee in Egypt?
Answer: Was Jesus Christ an immigrant or a refugee in Egypt? This question most likely refers to the fact that Joseph and Mary took their young son Jesus and fled to Egypt. Joseph was warned by an angel that Herod would attempt to kill Jesus and indeed, after they fled, Herod sent soldiers to murder all of the baby boys ages 3 and under. While the family did flee to Egypt, they were not refugees. Egypt, like Jerusalem and many other locations in Europe and Africa, belonged to the Roman Empire. Therefore the family was essentially traveling within one “country”. Jesus and his parents were neither refugees nor immigrants, they were lawful residents of the Roman Empire.

Question: Should Black people once again start using their 2nd Amendment rights to defend themselves from government tyranny (police brutality), basically like what the Black Panthers did in the 1960s?
Answer: Should Black people once again start using their 2nd Amendment rights to defend themselves from government tyranny (police brutality), basically like what the Black Panthers did in the 1960s? Every eligible and capable American should exercise their 2nd Amendment rights. The 2nd Amendment is a protection of the right of self-defense, not a protection of the right to form a vengeful mob and look for vigilante justice. I know several Black Americans who already carry a gun (legally). Most people who carry firearms do not have an issue with police as they are law abiding citizens. Depending upon the state, the laws put in place to carry a gun can be extensive. In Texas, one must take (and pass) a written exam on gun safety, a shooting proficiency test, and a federal background check. The background check eliminates the eligibility to carry if there are any felony convictions or certain other crimes, delinquent payments in federal taxes, student loans, or child support. Each state has its own laws concerning gun ownership and the ability to carry that firearm. The problem we are facing is that we, as a culture, no longer respect the law or the police. The actions of a few terrible officers have been highlighted by the media and have destroyed much of the credibility of police in general. Culturally we are also not taught the skills we need to interact with law enforcement. As a result, officers now fear for their lives even when performing common functions of their job. Police have been trapped, ambushed, and killed on routine stops. In fact, many times the most dangerous job for an officer is a routine traffic stop. This only fuels problems when people resist arrest as adrenaline is already pumping during an altercation. https://www.fbi.gov/file-repository/ucr/2020-leoka-infographic.pdf What needs to be done is that people need to be aware of their rights. Too many of us watch too much Law and Order and assume we know the law. Know the laws in your state, stay calm, answer questions, be respectful and pay attention. If an officer is disrespectful or inappropriate, report it and follow up to the proper authorities. Everybody, regardless of color, creed, or religion, has the right to self-defense. Everyone who is legally able to do so should take the time, initiative, and expense purchase a firearm and train on how to use it. If the time ever comes when we as Americans must stand against true tyranny, whether it be government or the police, we should be at the ready.
